solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Resist awkward member of the family

indicators.note: something awkward is out of shape, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

explanation.surface: A difficult relative refuses to cooperate.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister is a female sibling, one of the closest relations in a household.

clue.text: Workplace in American institute, insecure on the outside

indicators.note: says the word for insecure wraps around the institute's letters

parts.note: an insecure person is shy, lacking confidence
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone works at an American university while feeling unsure of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A smithy is a blacksmith's forge, the place where metal is worked.

clue.text: Course for which one must bring in black dishes

indicators.note: the course word must take the black letter inside it

parts.note: a syllabus is a course of study
B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A menu note says a course requires dark-coloured dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests a meal course, but here it is a course of study; SYLLABUBS are creamy desserts.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabubs are whipped cream-and-wine desserts, so they are dishes served at a meal.

clue.text: Punctilious editor required

parts.note: punctilious means precise, exact

explanation.surface: A fussy editor was in demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact something is to demand or require it, so exacted is a past-tense synonym of required.

clue.text: Seeming to be a quiet dad maybe

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
a dad is an example of a parent, hence the maybe

explanation.surface: Someone appears to be a calm father.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means seeming so on the surface, as in an apparent contradiction.

clue.text: Steak and beer brought to the Lords?

parts.note: porter is a dark beer
the House of Lords is the upper chamber of the UK Parliament

explanation.surface: Dinner and a pint delivered to the peers in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lords is the UK Parliament's upper chamber, so 'the Lords' can be called the House.
explanation.definitionFit: A porterhouse is a large cut of beef steak from the short loin.

clue.text: Draw a large area of land for the audience

indicators.note: what an audience hears is spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than written

parts.note: a tract is a large area of land, giving a tract

explanation.surface: Sketch a wide stretch of countryside for spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a crowd is to attract it, pulling people in.

clue.text: Escape from senior member right away outside university

indicators.note: the shortened senior word sits around the university letter
right away tells us to drop the letter for right from the senior member

parts.note: an elder is a senior member of a church or tribe

explanation.surface: A senior figure flees at once from a campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately' but means remove R: ELDER loses R to become ELDE, which goes around U.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude is to escape from or evade someone.

clue.text: Modish types upsetting resident

indicators.note: upsetting knocks things over, so the following word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fashionable newcomers annoy a local.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendies are people who follow fashion, a colloquial term for stylish types.

clue.text: Bad influence? Couldn't agree more!

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects
to have a say is to have influence

explanation.surface: Someone warns of a corrupting presence and another person heartily concurs.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a British idiom of emphatic agreement, like 'absolutely!'.

clue.text: Push out rubbish for moralist to consume

indicators.note: the moralist swallows the rubbish word, taking it inside

parts.note: a prude is a priggish moralist
rot means rubbish, nonsense

explanation.surface: A stern moralist is made to put out the garbage.
explanation.definitionFit: To protrude is to stick out or project beyond a surface.

clue.text: Listen to army fighter in South America suffering

parts.note: to hear is to listen to
TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve
Che Guevara was a guerrilla fighter in South America

explanation.surface: Pay attention to a soldier in a South American war who is in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional suffering or grief.

clue.text: Things that are sure to bring particular obligations

parts.note: certain means particular, as in certain people
ties are obligations or bonds

explanation.surface: Some commitments are guaranteed to arise.
explanation.definitionFit: Certainties are things known for sure, dead certs.

clue.text: A body part in the van

parts.note: the head is a part of the body

explanation.surface: A piece of a body found in a delivery vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The van here is the vanguard, the front, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the van, short for vanguard, is to be in front, out in front.

clue.text: Secret lad, he involved with brunette

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled together, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A young man is quietly having an affair with a dark-haired woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Done under the table means done secretly, often illicitly, an idiom for covert dealing.

clue.text: Polluted bar seemed horrible

indicators.note: horrible suggests something gone badly wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A pub looked revolting and dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: Besmeared means smeared all over or soiled, close to dirtied or polluted.

clue.text: Magnificent object in second place I had

indicators.note: the object word goes inside the run of second, place and I had

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
I'd is the contraction of I had
an end is an object or aim

explanation.surface: A grand item was where I came second.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid means magnificent, impressively grand.

clue.text: Students troubled as tutor gasped

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Learners are worried when their teacher gasps in shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Postgraduates are students studying after a first degree.

clue.text: Good little creatures shine

parts.note: a litter is a brood of young animals

explanation.surface: Fine young animals gleam.
explanation.definitionFit: To glitter is to shine with sparkling light.

clue.text: First female to get into this bunch of crooks

indicators.note: the first woman's name goes inside the word this

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: The original woman joins this gang of criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieves are a band of crooks who steal.

clue.text: Snake outside shelter unaware of what's going on

indicators.note: the snake word goes around the shelter word

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
lee is shelter, the side away from the wind

explanation.surface: A snake lies outside a refuge, oblivious.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone asleep is unconscious and so oblivious to events around them.

clue.text: Boredom in kindergarten — nuisance!

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A child at nursery school is a pest, causing tedium.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French-derived word for listless boredom.

clue.text: They're seen in churches, and they sound like wicked chaps

indicators.note: says the answer is said the same as a word for rogues

parts.note: knaves are dishonest, villainous men

explanation.surface: Something found in churches is pronounced like a word for scoundrels.
explanation.definitionFit: The nave is the central part of a church where the congregation sits.

clue.text: Poverty seen around — has a meal to be brought in?

indicators.note: the eating word is put inside the turned word
says seen is turned back to front

parts.note: to dine is to have a meal, so dines

explanation.surface: Want is visible everywhere; must food be delivered?
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen' looks like part of the surface's description of poverty, but 'around' turns it backwards, and 'to be brought in' puts the meal word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Neediness is the state of being in want, close to poverty.

clue.text: Party with very little Ecstasy? Then end getting joint

parts.note: a do is a party
V is the short form of very, so very little means very cut down
E is slang for the drug Ecstasy
a tail is an end

explanation.surface: A party with hardly any drugs, then a finish that gets a spliff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' tempts as a cannabis cigarette; here it is a woodworking joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovetail is an interlocking woodworking joint with fan-shaped tenons.

clue.text: A bit of the Bible making one hostile

parts.note: a verse is a short numbered section of the Bible

explanation.surface: A Bible passage turns someone antagonistic.
explanation.definitionFit: Averse means opposed to or hostile towards something.

clue.text: Daughter is wanting long hair, the pain!

parts.note: a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: A girl wants long locks, which is agony for the parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is mental or physical suffering, the same as pain.

clue.text: American political party, being full of energy, got through

indicators.note: the American and party letters together hold the energy letter

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A lively American party consumed something.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland; 'being full of' puts the energy letter inside the combined American and party letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Used up means consumed entirely, gone through.
